q: Which pair of adverse effects is particularly associated with levothyroxine overreplacement in older adults?
o: Atrial fibrillation and loss of bone
Bradycardia and loss of bone
Atrial fibrillation and increased bone mass
Bradycardia and increased bone mass
explanation:
**Iatrogenic hyperthyroidism** is a risk of excessive thyroid hormone replacement (p. 1552). Its adverse effects parallel endogenous hyperthyroidism, "most notably atrial fibrillation and bone loss"; careful titration and monitoring reduce overreplacement risk (p. 1552).

**A. Atrial fibrillation and loss of bone.** Correct, This is the pair of risks explicitly emphasized for iatrogenic hyperthyroidism (p. 1552).
**B. Bradycardia and loss of bone.** Wrong, Bone loss fits, but the cardiac risk emphasized is atrial fibrillation; bradycardia is described with profound hypothyroidism (p. 1552).
**C. Atrial fibrillation and increased bone mass.** Wrong, Atrial fibrillation fits, but the source identifies bone loss rather than increased bone mass (p. 1552).
**D. Bradycardia and increased bone mass.** Wrong, The source emphasizes atrial fibrillation and bone loss; bradycardia belongs to its description of profound hypothyroidism (p. 1552).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1552.
label: Source: hazzard marked .pdf · 1552

q: מהו ייפוי כוח מתמשך (Enduring Power of Attorney) לפי חוק הכשרות המשפטית 2016?
o: מסמך שממנה אדם כשיר (מיופה כוח) לקבל החלטות בעניינו כשייאבד כשירות, בתחומים שנקבעו מראש
צו שבו בית המשפט ממנה נציג לעניינים האישיים והרכושיים לאחר הגשת בקשה, בלי שהאדם ערך מסמך מינוי מראש
הסכם שבו הצוות הרפואי בוחר נציג למטופל לפי מצבו בזמן האשפוז, בלי שהמטופל קבע מראש את האדם והסמכויות
מסמך בנקאי רגיל שמסמיך את הבנק למנות נציג לקבלת החלטות רפואיות לאחר שהלקוח אינו מסוגל להבין בענייניו
explanation:
**ייפוי כוח מתמשך מבטא בחירה מראש של האדם** במי שיפעל בענייניו כאשר לא יוכל להבין ולקבל החלטות בתחום שנקבע. הבחירה נשענת על אמון ורצון חופשי, וניתן להגדיר עניינים אישיים, רפואיים ורכושיים. אין מדובר בנציג שנבחר עבורו רק לאחר שהתעורר הצורך (עמ׳ 4, 10).
"ייפוי כוח מתמשך הוא מסמך משפטי המאפשר לך לתכנן את עתידך בשלב שבו הנך בעל יכולת ומסוגלות לקבל החלטות ולבצע פעולות." (עמ׳ 4).

**א. מסמך שממנה אדם כשיר (מיופה כוח) לקבל החלטות בעניינו כשייאבד כשירות, בתחומים שנקבעו מראש.** נכונה, האדם בוחר מראש מיופה כוח ואת תחומי הסמכות, כך שהפעולה העתידית נשענת על בחירתו ולא על מינוי אוטומטי בידי גורם אחר (עמ׳ 4, 10).
**ב. צו שבו בית המשפט ממנה נציג לעניינים האישיים והרכושיים לאחר הגשת בקשה, בלי שהאדם ערך מסמך מינוי מראש.** שגויה, האפשרות מתארת מינוי בידי בית המשפט לאחר הגשת בקשה, ואילו המסמך הנדון מבוסס על בחירת הממנה ותכנון מוקדם שלו (עמ׳ 4).
**ג. הסכם שבו הצוות הרפואי בוחר נציג למטופל לפי מצבו בזמן האשפוז, בלי שהמטופל קבע מראש את האדם והסמכויות.** שגויה, בחירת הנציג בידי הצוות אינה בחירת הממנה. לכן הסכם כזה אינו ממלא את עקרון הבחירה האישית שעליו נשען ייפוי כוח מתמשך (עמ׳ 4).
**ד. מסמך בנקאי רגיל שמסמיך את הבנק למנות נציג לקבלת החלטות רפואיות לאחר שהלקוח אינו מסוגל להבין בענייניו.** שגויה, מסמך בנקאי רגיל אינו ההסדר המתואר: סמכות בעניינים רפואיים נכללת בתחום אישי או רפואי שהממנה מגדיר, ולא נובעת מבחירת נציג בידי הבנק (עמ׳ 4, 10).

מקור: משרד המשפטים, מדריך לממנה בייפוי כוח מתמשך, עמ׳ 4, 6, 10, 12.
ref: מדריך לממנה - ייפוי כוח מתמשך · PDF pp4,6,10
label: Source: מדריך לממנה - ייפוי כוח מתמשך · PDF pp4,6,10

q: A 73-year-old woman with an ulcerated 6-mm nodular basal cell carcinoma on her nose is considering Mohs surgery. Which description explains local tumor control with tissue preservation?
o: Electrodessication and curettage examine the entire margin microscopically during tissue removal
Mohs surgery selects margins by appearance and postpones their microscopic examination
Mohs examines complete margins in real time during staged excision
Electrodessication and curettage map residual margin cells to guide further targeted excision
explanation:
**Mohs micrographic surgery** uses staged excision with real-time microscopic evaluation of the entire surgical margin. Residual tumor is mapped to guide the next excision, allowing preservation of normal tissue while pursuing clear margins (p. 1462).
"serial tangential excisions with real-time microscopic evaluation of the entirety of the surgical margins to ensure that the tumor is excised completely." (p. 1462).
"If residual cancer cells are noted at a margin, the precise location is mapped and identified on the patient." (p. 1462).

**A. Electrodessication and curettage examine the entire margin microscopically during tissue removal.** Wrong, electrodessication and curettage remove gross tumor and destroy residual cells at the wound base and periphery; the complete microscopic margin method described belongs to Mohs surgery (pp. 1461–1462).
**B. Mohs surgery selects margins by appearance and postpones their microscopic examination.** Wrong, Mohs uses real-time microscopic examination to guide subsequent stages, not delayed examination after visually chosen margins (p. 1462).
**C. Mohs examines complete margins in real time during staged excision.** Correct, the staged, complete-margin examination is the mechanism the source links to tissue preservation and local control (p. 1462).
**D. Electrodessication and curettage map residual margin cells to guide further targeted excision.** Wrong, mapping residual cancer at a margin and excising the corresponding location is the Mohs technique, not the curettage-and-desiccation sequence (pp. 1461–1462).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1461, 1462.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp.1461–1462

q: A woman taking metformin is hospitalized with a severe acute illness that reduces tissue perfusion. Which risk explains avoiding metformin in this setting?
o: Lactic acidosis in the setting of reduced tissue perfusion
Excess insulin in the setting of pancreatic stimulation
Metabolic alkalosis in the setting of increased acid loss
Fluid overload in the setting of increased sodium retention
explanation:
**Lactic acidosis** is the complication underlying this precaution. Although rare with metformin, it is the stated concern during major acute illness with impaired tissue perfusion (p. 1576). The source identifies "decreased tissue perfusion as a precipitating factor for lactic acidosis." (p. 1576).

**A. Lactic acidosis in the setting of reduced tissue perfusion.** Correct, the source explicitly connects reduced perfusion during major illness with the lactic-acidosis risk underlying avoidance of metformin (p. 1576).
**B. Excess insulin in the setting of pancreatic stimulation.** Wrong, the precaution asked about concerns lactic acidosis with impaired perfusion, rather than excess insulin from pancreatic stimulation (p. 1576).
**C. Metabolic alkalosis in the setting of increased acid loss.** Wrong, the source identifies lactic acidosis, rather than alkalosis from acid loss, as the complication relevant to this setting (p. 1576).
**D. Fluid overload in the setting of increased sodium retention.** Wrong, sodium retention is not the risk on which this stated metformin precaution is based; the source specifies lactic acidosis (p. 1576).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1576.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: A 79-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation, no mechanical valve, and no significant mitral stenosis cannot maintain a therapeutic INR on warfarin. A switch to apixaban is planned. She weighs 55 kg and has a serum creatinine of 1.8 mg/dL. According to Table 77-8, how should these findings affect dose selection?
o: Use the standard dose because she is younger than eighty years
Use the reduced dose because of her weight and serum creatinine
Use the standard dose because the age and weight criteria do not coincide
Use less than the reduced dose because two reduction criteria are present
explanation:
**Apixaban dose reduction** in Table 77-8 depends on meeting at least two of the listed criteria, not on meeting the age criterion in particular. The table specifies "2.5 mg twice daily (for at least two criteria)" (p. 1205). Applied to the stem, low body weight and elevated creatinine meet two criteria despite her age.

**A. Use the standard dose because she is younger than eighty years.** Wrong, age below the listed threshold does not cancel the two qualifying weight and creatinine findings (p. 1205).
**B. Use the reduced dose because of her weight and serum creatinine.** Correct, her weight is below 60 kg and her creatinine is at least 1.5 mg/dL, meeting the table’s two-criterion rule (p. 1205).
**C. Use the standard dose because the age and weight criteria do not coincide.** Wrong, the rule permits weight and creatinine to supply the two criteria; it does not require the age and weight criteria together (p. 1205).
**D. Use less than the reduced dose because two reduction criteria are present.** Wrong, two criteria trigger the specified reduced dose; the table does not prescribe a further reduction for this combination (p. 1205).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1205.
ref: Hazzard Ch 77 — CARDIAC ARRHYTHMIAS · Harrison Ch 286 — ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction

q: A patient with postoperative delirium continues to endanger himself and interrupt essential treatment despite nonpharmacologic measures. Medication for symptom control is judged necessary. Which prescribing principle should guide treatment?
o: Use a high starting dose and continue it routinely to prevent recurrence
Use a high starting dose and reduce it after achieving deep sedation
Use the lowest starting dose for the shortest possible duration
Use a fixed dose and continue it after recovery to prevent future confusion
explanation:
**Symptom medication** can itself worsen mental status and prolong delirium, so its use requires balancing benefit against adverse effects (p. 888). The source states, "Any drug should be initiated at the lowest starting dose for the shortest time possible." (p. 888).

**A. Use a high starting dose and continue it routinely to prevent recurrence.** Wrong, High initial dosing and routine continuation increase exposure beyond the low-dose, short-duration principle (p. 888; application).
**B. Use a high starting dose and reduce it after achieving deep sedation.** Wrong, Deep sedation is not the stated aim; the clinical endpoint is an awake but manageable patient (p. 889).
**C. Use the lowest starting dose for the shortest possible duration.** Correct, This follows the source’s instruction while addressing the severe symptoms that have disrupted essential care (p. 888).
**D. Use a fixed dose and continue it after recovery to prevent future confusion.** Wrong, The source calls for continued reassessment and tapering off as soon as possible, not maintenance after recovery (p. 889).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 888, 889.
ref: Hazzard Ch 58 — DELIRIUM· Harrison Ch 26 — Neurologic Causes of Weakness and Paralysis

q: An 84-year-old woman has dysuria and urinary frequency without fever, flank pain, or systemic symptoms. Creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. Urine culture grows E. coli susceptible to nitrofurantoin, ciprofloxacin, and amoxicillin-clavulanate but resistant to TMP-SMX. Which oral agent is the appropriate first-line choice for acute simple cystitis according to Hazzard?
o: Ciprofloxacin as first-line treatment based on culture susceptibility
Nitrofurantoin as first-line treatment based on culture susceptibility
TMP-SMX as first-line treatment based on the clinical diagnosis
Amoxicillin-clavulanate as first-line treatment based on culture susceptibility
explanation:
**Nitrofurantoin** is a first-line option for acute simple cystitis when the organism is susceptible and creatinine clearance is at least 30 mL/min. The chapter lists amoxicillin-clavulanate and fluoroquinolones as second-line options; known susceptibility also matters when selecting therapy (pp. 1708–1709).
"nitrofurantoin remains a good option for treatment of acute simple cystitis in older adults with creatinine clearance greater than or equal to 30 mL/min." (p. 1709).
"FQs are no longer considered first-line treatment of acute simple cystitis because of increasing resistance against gram-negative pathogens and serious side effects associated with its use." (p. 1709).

**A. Ciprofloxacin as first-line treatment based on culture susceptibility.** Wrong, fluoroquinolones are no longer first-line treatment for simple cystitis because of resistance and serious adverse effects, despite the susceptibility reported here (p. 1709).
**B. Nitrofurantoin as first-line treatment based on culture susceptibility.** Correct, the stem describes simple cystitis, a susceptible organism, and renal clearance above the source's threshold (p. 1709).
**C. TMP-SMX as first-line treatment based on the clinical diagnosis.** Wrong, the culture in the stem documents resistance; selection should incorporate susceptibility rather than relying on the syndrome alone (p. 1708).
**D. Amoxicillin-clavulanate as first-line treatment based on culture susceptibility.** Wrong, the chapter places this agent among second-line choices, while a suitable first-line agent is available here (p. 1709).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1708, 1709.
ref: Hazzard Ch 106 — URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS· Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease

q: An 84-year-old woman with moderate vascular dementia and diabetes is transferred from her nursing home after developing increased confusion and falls over two days. Mirtazapine 15 mg nightly was started a week ago for depression and poor appetite. She is somnolent, with blood pressure falling from 140/80 supine to 110/65 standing and mild cogwheeling. Sodium is 128 mEq/L, glucose 180 mg/dL, and creatinine 1.8 mg/dL. Which mirtazapine-related risk and monitoring approach is supported by Beers 2023?
o: Possible SIADH or hyponatremia; monitor sodium closely after initiation
Possible SIADH or hyponatremia; reserve sodium checks for established long-term treatment
Protection against SIADH or hyponatremia; monitor sodium closely after initiation
Protection against SIADH or hyponatremia; reserve sodium checks for established long-term treatment
explanation:
**Mirtazapine requires caution for SIADH or hyponatremia**. Beers recommends close sodium monitoring when treatment is started or the dose changes (p. 2068). "May exacerbate or cause SIADH or hyponatremia; monitor sodium levels closely when starting or changing dosages in older adults." (p. 2068). This identifies a relevant medication risk without establishing the sole cause of this patient's deterioration.

**A. Possible SIADH or hyponatremia; monitor sodium closely after initiation.** Correct, This captures both the recognized risk and monitoring near initiation, which is the timing in the stem (p. 2068).
**B. Possible SIADH or hyponatremia; reserve sodium checks for established long-term treatment.** Wrong, The risk is correct, but delaying sodium checks misses the starting or changing treatment period highlighted by Beers (p. 2068).
**C. Protection against SIADH or hyponatremia; monitor sodium closely after initiation.** Wrong, Close monitoring is appropriate, but Beers describes potential causation or worsening rather than protection (p. 2068).
**D. Protection against SIADH or hyponatremia; reserve sodium checks for established long-term treatment.** Wrong, Both the protective claim and postponing checks conflict with the stated risk and recommendation (p. 2068).

Source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023, pp. 2068.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING· Harrison Ch 433 — Approach to the Patient with Neurologic Disease

q: An 86-year-old man is readmitted with advanced lung disease. He is receiving treatment for an exacerbation but has severe symptoms and unclear goals of care. He is alert and wants to understand his options. When is palliative care consultation appropriate?
o: After a hospice decision and discontinuation of disease treatment
After further deterioration identifies the final days of life
During this admission for symptom relief and goal clarification
At discharge planning after the current exacerbation has been treated
explanation:
**Palliative care** can be integrated during hospitalization to address symptom burden and clarify goals. Hazzard describes integration at all stages of illness, including help with complex medical decisions (p. 1082).
"palliative care can be successfully integrated for critically ill patients at all stages of illness." (p. 1082).

**A. After a hospice decision and discontinuation of disease treatment.** Wrong, Integration is not restricted to a prior hospice decision; the present symptom burden and need for goal clarification already fit the described role (p. 1082).
**B. After further deterioration identifies the final days of life.** Wrong, Waiting for the final days would miss the source's broader role across stages of illness (p. 1082).
**C. During this admission for symptom relief and goal clarification.** Correct, The current admission provides the setting to address both symptoms and the unresolved treatment goals (p. 1082).
**D. At discharge planning after the current exacerbation has been treated.** Wrong, The source describes inpatient integration, including consultation on admission, rather than requiring completion of exacerbation treatment first (p. 1082).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1082.
chapterTitle: Palliative Care and Special Management Issues
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp.1052, 1082, Figure 70-3

q: An 84-year-old nursing-home resident with severe COPD, moderate vascular dementia (MMSE 18), and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73 m²) presents with acute dyspnea. He is uncomfortable but follows simple commands. His MOLST specifies no intubation but permits bilevel positive airway pressure. Arterial blood gases show pH 7.28, PaCO2 68 mm Hg, and PaO2 58 mm Hg; chest radiography shows no infiltrate. His son asks about comfort-focused care. Which initial ventilatory approach is supported by the source and the stated treatment preferences?
o: Favor oxygen therapy without ventilatory support for the respiratory acidosis
Favor bilevel noninvasive ventilation after assessing for relevant contraindications
Favor withholding ventilatory support because the directive declines intubation
Favor endotracheal intubation to address the hypercapnic respiratory failure
explanation:
**Noninvasive positive pressure ventilation** is indicated for COPD exacerbations with acute hypercapnia and respiratory acidosis when contraindications are absent. It supports ventilation while medical treatment takes effect; invasive ventilation must also be consistent with the person's goals of care (pp. 1257, 1261).
"NPPV (usually bilevel positive airway pressure [BPAP]) is indicated for persons with acute exacerbations of COPD associated with acute hypercarbia" (p. 1257).

**A. Favor oxygen therapy without ventilatory support for the respiratory acidosis.** Wrong, the source favors adding noninvasive ventilatory support in acute hypercapnic COPD exacerbations with respiratory acidosis when appropriate, rather than relying on medical therapy alone (p. 1257).
**B. Favor bilevel noninvasive ventilation after assessing for relevant contraindications.** Correct, the gas results match the described indication, and the stem explicitly permits this form of support; contraindications still require assessment (p. 1257).
**C. Favor withholding ventilatory support because the directive declines intubation.** Wrong, the stem distinguishes refusal of intubation from acceptance of noninvasive support; goals of care constrain the invasive option (p. 1261).
**D. Favor endotracheal intubation to address the hypercapnic respiratory failure.** Wrong, invasive ventilation would conflict with the explicit no-intubation preference; the source makes intubation contingent on goals of care (p. 1261).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1257, 1261.
ref: Hazzard Ch 7 — DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST· Harrison Ch 295 — Approach to the Patient with Disease of the Respiratory System
chapterTitle: DECISION MAKING AND ADVANCE CARE PLANNING: WHAT MATTERS MOST

q: A 77-year-old woman with moderate COPD and frailty has lost 15 lb unintentionally, reports exhaustion, and has a grip strength of 15 kg. She has temporal wasting and reduced breath sounds, uses tiotropium and as-needed albuterol, and has had progressive breathlessness for two weeks. She is unable to climb to her bedroom and sleeps in a recliner; her daughter is considering nursing-home placement. After evaluation of her recent deterioration and stabilization of her respiratory illness, which rehabilitation plan directly addresses exercise limitation and nutritional needs?
o: Provide dietary counseling while substituting rest for exercise training
Combine pulmonary rehabilitation with individualized assessment of nutritional needs
Provide inhaler education while deferring physical reconditioning
Provide nutritional supplements while deferring supervised exercise training
explanation:
**Pulmonary rehabilitation** includes assessment, supervised exercise, reconditioning, and education (p. 1258). It addresses physical deconditioning as well as respiratory symptoms; nutritional treatment should be based on dietary assessment when muscle loss is present (pp. 737, 1258). "The process of PR includes patient assessment, supervised exercise training and reconditioning, patient education, and outcome assessment." (p. 1258).

**A. Provide dietary counseling while substituting rest for exercise training.** Wrong, substituting rest omits the exercise training and reconditioning included in pulmonary rehabilitation (p. 1258).
**B. Combine pulmonary rehabilitation with individualized assessment of nutritional needs.** Correct, this combines the rehabilitation components with attention to dietary intake in a patient with weight loss and muscle wasting (pp. 737, 1258).
**C. Provide inhaler education while deferring physical reconditioning.** Wrong, education is a component, but the source also includes supervised exercise and reconditioning (p. 1258).
**D. Provide nutritional supplements while deferring supervised exercise training.** Wrong, supplements may be considered when dietary intake is insufficient; they do not supply the exercise component of pulmonary rehabilitation (pp. 737, 1258).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 737, 1258.
ref: Hazzard Ch 49 — MUSCLE AGING AND SARCOPENIA· Harrison Ch 295 — Approach to the Patient with Disease of the Respiratory System

q: An older woman newly diagnosed with metastatic breast cancer has symptoms and is continuing oncologic assessment and treatment. When does Hazzard recommend considering palliative care?
o: When dependence on other people becomes complete
After the available oncologic treatments are exhausted
During the transition to care in the final days
Early in the course alongside oncologic treatment
explanation:
**Early palliative care** can be integrated with cancer treatment. The chapter reports improved quality of life with this integration and recommends considering consultation early for older patients with metastatic breast cancer, preferably at diagnosis (p. 1406).
"integrating palliative care with standard cancer treatment, including chemotherapy, can lead to significant improvements in quality of life and even survival." (p. 1406).
"a palliative care consultation be considered for all older patients with metastatic breast cancer and symptomatic patients with early breast cancer early in their course" (p. 1406).

**A. When dependence on other people becomes complete.** Wrong, complete dependency is not the proposed trigger; the source recommends consultation early in metastatic disease (p. 1406).
**B. After the available oncologic treatments are exhausted.** Wrong, the source supports integration with standard cancer treatment, including chemotherapy, rather than waiting for its exhaustion (p. 1406).
**C. During the transition to care in the final days.** Wrong, palliative care is explicitly distinguished from end-of-life care and can start earlier (p. 1406).
**D. Early in the course alongside oncologic treatment.** Correct, this follows the recommendation for early consultation alongside cancer treatment (p. 1406).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1406.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES· Harrison Ch 79 — Infections in Patients with Cancer
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: A 78-year-old man with a low income, diabetes, and heart failure has been hospitalized three times in the past year. His primary care physician is considering GRACE. Which description matches this model?
o: A postdischarge visiting team that concludes its work after the initial home assessment
A nurse practitioner–social worker team combining home assessment with interdisciplinary coordination
An outpatient rehabilitation team providing an intensive course of supervised physiotherapy
A specialist coordination team reviewing records without direct assessment of the patient
explanation:
**GRACE** integrates geriatric and primary care for low-income older adults. A nurse practitioner and social worker assess the patient at home, and their findings are reviewed with an interdisciplinary team and the primary care physician (pp. 200–201). "Their findings and recommendations are reviewed by the interdisciplinary team and discussed with the primary care physician." (p. 201)

**A. A postdischarge visiting team that concludes its work after the initial home assessment.** Wrong, The source describes annual assessment and ongoing coordinated management, not completion after one postdischarge visit (pp. 200–201).
**B. A nurse practitioner–social worker team combining home assessment with interdisciplinary coordination.** Correct, This captures the home-based support team and its collaboration with primary care and the interdisciplinary team (pp. 200–201).
**C. An outpatient rehabilitation team providing an intensive course of supervised physiotherapy.** Wrong, Physical therapy is represented within the wider team, but GRACE addresses medical, functional, and psychosocial needs rather than being a physiotherapy course (p. 201).
**D. A specialist coordination team reviewing records without direct assessment of the patient.** Wrong, The nurse practitioner and social worker directly perform in-home CGA; record review without patient assessment omits that component (pp. 200–201).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 200, 201.
chapterTitle: Models of Hospital and Outpatient Care
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp. 200–201, GRACE

q: במטופל עם פצע לחץ ללא חסרים תזונתיים, איזה תוסף תזונתי נמצא כמסייע לרפוי פצע אם ניתן לפחות 4 שבועות?
o: ויטמין A
ויטמין C
ברזל
אבץ
explanation:
The source includes **zinc as part of a combined supplement** providing high energy and protein together with arginine, antioxidants and micronutrients. It does not establish the benefit of zinc alone without deficiency. Benefit is described when the combined supplement is given for more than four weeks, and no zinc sulfate dose is supplied (Hazzard 8e, p. 692).

**A. Vitamin A.** Wrong, the source provides no evidence that vitamin A supplementation improves pressure-injury healing without a specific deficiency; the stem provides no such deficiency (p. 692).
**B. Vitamin C.** Wrong, vitamin C is also among supplements without proven healing benefit in the absence of a specific deficiency (p. 692).
**C. Iron.** Wrong, iron is covered by the same statement of no demonstrated benefit without a specific deficiency, whereas the stem states that deficiencies are absent (p. 692).
**D. Zinc.** Correct for scoring under the official key. The source supports zinc within a combined supplement, not zinc alone in a patient without deficiency (p. 692).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 692.

q: Which approach best fits a nursing-home resident with diabetes, substantial disability and limited life expectancy?
o: Pursue stringent A1C targets as the main priority despite disability and limited prognosis.
Assume supervised medication administration removes the practical risk from hypoglycemia.
Use restrictive diets to normalize glucose even when maintaining nutritional intake is difficult.
Individualize basic diabetes care around prognosis, nutrition and the facility's hypoglycemia risks.
explanation:
For many nursing-home residents with diabetes, **basic diabetes care** is more appropriate than stringent biochemical targets because disability and limited life expectancy change the balance of benefit and burden. Facility staffing and meal timing can also make hypoglycemia harder to recognize and manage. Goals should account for these limitations rather than pursue tight control by default (p1585).
"Because of the degree of disability and limited life expectancy of these patients, basic diabetes care should usually be the goal" (p1585).
"staff may be less trained to understand the risks associated with these agents and have limited ability to recognize and treat hypoglycemia rapidly." (p1585).

**A. Pursue stringent A1C targets as the main priority despite disability and limited prognosis.** Wrong, stringent goals conflict with the chapter's emphasis on basic care in residents with disability and limited life expectancy (p1585).
**B. Assume supervised medication administration removes the practical risk from hypoglycemia.** Wrong, staff may have limited ability to recognize or treat hypoglycemia, so medication administration does not make tight control safe (p1585).
**C. Use restrictive diets to normalize glucose even when maintaining nutritional intake is difficult.** Wrong, the chapter favors adequate nutrition and enjoyment rather than unnecessary dietary restrictions in residents with limited life expectancy (p1585).
**D. Individualize basic diabetes care around prognosis, nutrition and the facility's hypoglycemia risks.** Correct, this approach incorporates prognosis, disability and practical hypoglycemia risks into individualized care (p1585).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p1585.

q: What prognostic certification does the chapter describe for US Medicare hospice?
o: The hospice director alone certifies terminal illness and prognosis under 6 months if the disease runs its usual and expected course
An LCD automatically certifies terminal illness and prognosis under 6 months if the disease runs its usual and expected course
The attending physician and hospice director certify terminal illness and prognosis under 6 months if the disease runs its usual and expected course
The attending physician alone certifies terminal illness and prognosis under 6 months if the disease runs its usual and expected course
explanation:
Medicare hospice certification involves the attending physician and hospice medical director certifying terminal illness with prognosis under six months if the disease runs its usual and expected course (p1046).

D. The attending physician alone certifies terminal illness and prognosis under 6 months if the disease runs its usual and expected course: The described certification involves both physicians (p1046).
A. The hospice director alone certifies terminal illness and prognosis under 6 months if the disease runs its usual and expected course: The described certification involves both physicians (p1046).
B. An LCD automatically certifies terminal illness and prognosis under 6 months if the disease runs its usual and expected course: LCDs guide prognosis; they do not replace the described physician certification (p1046).
